title: Berkeley student banquet planning
full_query: Please make a plan for my student group's end of year banquet, including a specific venue and a specific menu from a caterer. We need a nice venue near Berkeley, CA with a projector for slides. There are around 30 people attending. We also need to cater food that accommodates the following dietary restrictions: 2 egg allergies, 2 peanut allergies, 1 dairy + nuts + shellfish allergy, and 1 vegetarian. The total budget for the banquet is 2500 dollars, with a hard cap of 3000 dollars. Do not factor in transportation in the budget.

pointwise.title: Specific nearby banquet venue
pointwise.question: Does the plan name a venue near Berkeley and describe a seated banquet arrangement for around 30 people?

anchors.1: No identifiable venue near Berkeley.
anchors.2: A venue is named without usable location or guest-capacity information.
anchors.3: Location and capacity or occasion suitability is materially unspecified; attractive surroundings do not compensate for an unclear seated arrangement.
anchors.4: Nearby location, a 30-person seated/table arrangement and concrete occasion suitability are clear, with only a minor room/layout detail missing.
anchors.5: Identifies a specific nearby venue and a seated/table arrangement for around 30, explaining concrete room or service features that suit a student end-of-year celebration.

pointwise.boundary: Do not impose an unrequested 10-mile radius, luxury standard or mandatory historic venue. Real-world claims are checked in D2, not assumed verified from naming. Occasion suitability must be concrete, not just the word nice; no luxury threshold.

provenance.change_note: v3.3 targeted revision: v3.3 retains this judgment object. Baseline mixed-performance check: New: identity, location and capacity define the selected venue; a beautiful venue with no dining capacity specified is 3, not offset by ambiance. Cross-review makes missing occasion suitability remain at 3 rather than allowing the old capacity-only 4.

pointwise.title: Projector arrangement
pointwise.question: Does the plan specify a usable projector arrangement for the group's slides?

anchors.2: Only a generic AV claim with no identifiable projection provision.
anchors.3: A projector is mentioned, but how it is obtained or used at the venue is materially unclear.
anchors.4: A venue-provided or arranged projector is identified, with a minor setup detail unconfirmed.
anchors.5: The plan identifies projection provision at the venue and the necessary screen/display surface and connection/setup assumptions, marking what still needs confirmation.

pointwise.boundary: A TV alone is not automatically a projector. Do not demand a particular projector model; quoted or budgeted rental is eligible when venue use is addressed.

provenance.change_note: Keep the projection requirement while allowing an explicitly arranged rental rather than only built-in equipment.

pointwise.title: Specific caterer and venue eligibility

anchors.2: A caterer is named but no service-area or venue relationship is stated.
anchors.3: Local service is stated but venue eligibility/outside-food permission is absent, or the reverse.
anchors.4: Service and venue policy fit are stated with a minor approval detail pending.
anchors.5: A specific local-serving caterer is paired with the venue, with outside-food or in-house-package eligibility explained and unconfirmed permissions clearly identified.

pointwise.boundary: A named provider with a real unresolved approval can form a conditional plan, but an unqualified compatibility assertion is not proof. No mandatory outside caterer.

provenance.change_note: Keep caterer-area and venue-policy relationship, allow in-house packages and transparent conditional approvals.

pointwise.title: Specific caterer menu

anchors.2: Only cuisine labels or an unattributed set of meal ideas.
anchors.3: Dishes are named, but major dishes are not tied to the caterer's menu or proposed substitutions are indistinguishable from actual offerings.
anchors.4: The selected menu is tied to the caterer with minor item or substitution ambiguity.
anchors.5: Identifiable dishes/packages form the proposed banquet meal; menu-listed items, proposed modifications and pending approvals are clearly distinguished.

pointwise.boundary: No compulsory plated service or appetizer-main-dessert sequence. Allergy suitability is separate; appealing dish descriptions are not evidence the caterer sells them.

provenance.change_note: Retain a specific real-provider menu; remove a prescribed elevated course format.

anchors.5: Maps adequate proposed meals to the two egg-allergy needs, distinguishes confirmed ingredients from pending caterer confirmation, and identifies a concrete resolution path for unknown ingredients.

pointwise.title: Budget components and assumptions
pointwise.question: Does the plan provide an interpretable breakdown of venue, catering and relevant event charges?

anchors.1: No usable budget.
anchors.2: Only an unexplained total or major costs omitted.
anchors.3: Venue and food appear, but a material fee, tax, tip, equipment cost or estimate basis is absent.
anchors.4: Main costs and applicable charges are itemized, with only a minor inclusion or estimate detail unclear.
anchors.5: The budget itemizes venue, food, applicable taxes/service/tip and other costs needed by the selected plan, distinguishing included, estimated, refundable and pending amounts without double counting.

pointwise.boundary: Only relevant costs are required; no mandatory decorations or insurance if not applicable. Price truth and arithmetic are audited in D2; meeting the cap is separate.

provenance.change_note: Keep cost breakdown and interpretability, remove the fixed 10% price tolerance in favor of scoped evidence checks.

pointwise.title: Target budget and hard cap
pointwise.question: Does the plan acknowledge the $2,500 target and keep its proposed all-in banquet budget within the $3,000 hard cap?

anchors.1: The recommended plan knowingly exceeds $3,000 without a viable correction.
anchors.2: The total cannot be assessed, or a claimed under-cap plan omits a major known charge.
anchors.3: An under-cap estimate is provided, but its important uncertainty could exceed the cap without a spending limit, or an over-$2,500 total is not acknowledged.
anchors.4: The stated all-in estimate and bounded remaining cost uncertainty fit within $3,000, and any spending above $2,500 is acknowledged; how a pending quote would be kept within its stated allowance is only partly explained.
anchors.5: The proposed all-in total is within $3,000; spending above $2,500 is explicitly identified, and pending quotes have limits or adjustments sufficient to preserve the cap.

pointwise.boundary: A hard cap permits exactly $3,000; the official 'strictly less' rule is not imposed. Do not reward spending more or less irrespective of the plan's requirements. An unbounded pending charge cannot qualify for 4 merely because the current estimate is below the cap. Use 3 when an important uncertainty could exceed the cap without a spending limit; 5 requires sufficient limits or adjustments for pending quotes. No pending quote is required to earn 5.

query_quotes: 2500 dollars, with a hard cap of 3000 dollars
provenance.change_note: Review 30: replace contradictory unbounded uncertainty at level 4 with bounded residual cost uncertainty; distinguish a stated allowance from sufficient quote limits/adjustments at level 5. Other anchors unchanged.

anchors.5: Relates venue access, setup/presentation and catering delivery/service to a proposed window, distinguishing operating hours from event availability and identifying the checks needed to confirm both providers.

pointwise.title: Booking conditions and next actions
pointwise.question: Does the plan identify consequential commitment conditions and concrete actions to resolve them before booking?

anchors.1: No booking conditions or next actions.
anchors.2: Only says book early or contact the vendors.
anchors.3: Gives concrete conditions without resolution actions, or specific actions that do not address the relevant price, availability or commitment uncertainties.
anchors.4: Connects the main pending commitment conditions to concrete confirmation actions, with only a minor applicable condition or confirmation detail missing.
anchors.5: Identifies applicable venue and caterer commitment conditions, separates known terms from unknowns, and explains what to confirm with the venue or caterer about availability, all-in prices and permissions before committing.

pointwise.boundary: No invented fees or actual contact required. Only applicable conditions are needed; state what needs checking rather than pretending an unknown term does not apply. Allergy-handling actions are PT.D1.08, not a second omission penalty here. Do not require named responsible people, a complete responsibility allocation or a deadline schedule. Actual vendor reservation windows or deadlines, when consequential to booking, are conditions to identify or confirm, not a requirement to invent an internal project timetable.

provenance.change_note: Review 30: remove owner and timetable requirements from high anchors; preserve concrete vendor confirmation actions and consequential applicable booking conditions.

official_disposition.reason: Retain an interpretable breakdown of applicable costs, not a guarantee of accurate prices or arithmetic. PT.D1.09 explicitly leaves truth and arithmetic to separate audits.

official_disposition.reason: Original negative weight penalizes transportation inclusion; do not reverse it.
official_disposition.discrimination_check: Original: The response provides a final budget which includes any transportation costs. PT.D1.11 penalizes attendee travel within the banquet budget, not food delivery.

official_disposition.reason: Keep $2,500 target and $3,000 cap, with exactly $3,000 allowed by the query.
official_disposition.discrimination_check: Original: The response provides a final post-tax and tip budget that is strictly less than $3000, and if the budget is more than $2500, the response acknowledges that it is over budget but under hard cap. PT.D1.10 detects over-cap or unacknowledged target overrun; strict-less-than-$3,000 behavior is intentionally not preserved. Level 4 requires bounded uncertainty within the cap; an unbounded material cost is not level 4. Level 5 retains sufficient quote limits or adjustments.

official_disposition.reason: Keep budget readability through actual lookup, not a compulsory table.
official_disposition.discrimination_check: Original: The response provides the final budget breakdown in a well structured format like a table for readability. PW.D6.02 distinguishes easy versus difficult budget-line retrieval; a clear list may perform as well as a table.

official_disposition.reason: Preserve applicable booking conditions and specific confirmation actions, without mandatory assignment of people or a complete deadline schedule.

Named owners and an internal timetable are not required for 5; consequential vendor timing still counts as an applicable condition.

author_notes: No old batch4 draft exists. New items follow the three-example division of labor without a fixed count.
Allergy meal allocation, vegetarian meal adequacy, food quantity and allergen handling are distinct checks; the combined dairy+nuts+shellfish restriction remains one simultaneous requirement.
